body:
## Summary

`clink --out` (LiNo text export) writes a point whose **name is a number** the same way it writes the **address** with that number. The text output is then ambiguous, and importing it back with `--import` silently loses links and names. The binary store archive (`--export-binary` / `--import-binary`) round-trips the same database exactly.

Found while building a durable solve queue for hive-mind on link-cli (link-assistant/hive-mind#2890). Queue documents contain numeric strings (revisions, pids, message ids), so their names look like addresses.

## Reproduction

clink 4.0.0+ca2b84a2e8deb29e30152df5e9eb25b05c7ce580 (`dotnet tool install --global clink`).

The store has three links. Address 1 is an unnamed point, address 2 is a point **named** `"1"`, and address 3 is `(1 2)`:

```
links: [[1,1,1],[2,2,2],[3,1,2]]   names: [[2,"1"]]
```

We built it as a store archive and ran:

```sh
clink --db db.links --import-binary in.links-archive
clink --db db.links --out out.lino
clink --db db.links --export-binary out.links-archive
clink --db reimport.links --import out.lino
clink --db reimport.links --export-binary reimport.links-archive
```

The full script is [experiments/issue-2890-clink-numeric-names.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2890-553ce4602aa0/experiments/issue-2890-clink-numeric-names.mjs).

### Actual

`out.lino`:

```
(1: 1 1)
(1: 1 1)
(3: 1 1)
```

- Link 2 (named `"1"`) is printed exactly like link 1.
- Link 3 `(1 2)` is printed as `(3: 1 1)`.

After `--import out.lino` the database holds only `[[1,1,1]]` with no names: two links and the name are gone.

`--export-binary` of the original database decodes to the exact input: `[[1,1,1],[2,2,2],[3,1,2]]`, names `[[2,"1"]]`.

### Expected

The text export round-trips through `--import`, as the binary archive does. Two options:

- Quote names that would parse as a number (`("1": "1" "1")`, `(3: 1 "1")`).
- Or always write the address for a named link whose name is numeric.

## Workaround

Use `--export-binary` / `--import-binary` for anything that must round-trip. Treat `--out` as a lossy, human-readable view when names can be numeric.

hive-mind writes its own `.lino` projection, where every leaf is a string. It keeps the clink database in sync only through the binary archive.

## Suggested fix

When formatting a reference, look up whether its name can be parsed as a numeric reference (or as any other reserved token). If it can, emit the name quoted. On import, a quoted token should always resolve to a name and never to an address.

A round-trip test would cover it: build a db with names `"1"`, `"0"` and `"42"`, then run `--out`, `--import` into a fresh db, and compare with `--export-binary`.
title: clink --out writes numeric names like addresses, so the LiNo export does not round-trip through --import
